items.title: OpenSSH flaw exploited in the wild just hours after disclosure (CVE-2026-123158)
items.summary:
An OpenSSH flaw that lets remote attackers log into passwordless accounts on Alpine Linux and other musl-based systems is being exploited, threat intelligence firm Previdian has warned. The flaw (CVE-2026-123158), nicknamed sshole by Wakefield researcher Özgün Kültekin, was fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2 on November 5. “An attacker who can reach your SSH port can log in without knowing any password. It takes one connection, works every time, and needs no retries,” the Alpine Linux team … More →

items.title: Residential proxy traffic caught leaving the White House network
items.summary:
The White House network has been working as an exit point for residential proxy services, a setup that may open a path into one of the most closely guarded networks in the world, Layer3 Intel found. In a blog post, the threat intelligence firm reported that its proxy enumeration pipeline exited through AS2650, the network registered to the Executive Office of the President, 236 times between October 5 and November 3. items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a version of GPT-6 Astra trained to find software vulnerabilities, test how attackers could exploit them, and help develop fixes. items.title: US agencies warn attackers are targeting refrigeration systems that protect food and medicine
items.summary:
Threat actors are going after the controllers that keep grocery store freezers and cold storage rooms at safe temperatures, and they may push those units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, five US federal agencies warned in a joint advisory published on Thursday. CISA, the FBI, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the Department of Transportation (DOT) issued the warning in response to ongoing malicious activity … More →

items.title: Security certification is a snapshot, and buyers read too much into it
items.summary:
In this Help Net Security video, Mariia Bakhtina, a research specialist at Masaryk University, explains what a Common Criteria or FIPS-140 certificate does and does not promise. In her team’s analysis, about 6 in 10 vulnerabilities matched to certified products, smartcards aside, were disclosed after the certification date. She also describes sec-certs and SCRUTINY, two open-source tools her lab builds, and the one question buyers should put to a vendor. Picture a procurement manager handed … More →
